parties:
Jahanara Ahmed ------ Appellant
vs.

full_judgment:
Md Ruhul Amin J: This appeal by leave has been preferred by respondent No. 5 of the writ petition No. 1289 of 1996 against the judgment and order dated 5th March, 1998 of a Division Bench of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute and thereupon declaring the Memorandum No. 448/Pro-Ka-Shi dated 15th August, 1994 issued by the Administrative Officer (respondent No. 5) Shahjalal Housing Estate, Sylhet intimating cancellation of the allotment letter No. 2639 dated 29-09-1983 in respect of the Plot No. 17, at Road No. 21 of Block-B and lease deed No. 3 dated 08-09-1985. 

 2. Facts, in short, are that writ petitioner-respondent No. 1 got allotment of residential plot No. 17 at Road No. 21, Block-B, of the Shahjalal Housing Estate, Sylhet on 29th September, 1983 for a consideration of Taka 65,071.80. As per stipulation of the allotment letter total amount of consideration money was to be paid in 4 installments. Respondent No. 1 on payment of 1st instalment amounting Taka 19,600.00 on 27th October 1983 got possession of the plot on 18th August 1985. The lease deed for 99 years was registered on 8th September, 1985. The respondent No. 1 paid two other instalments i.e. 2nd and 3rd instalments of the consideration money. On 1st June, 1995 the constituted Attorney of the respondent No. 1 went to deposit the amount of the 4th instalment, but the same was not accepted on the plea of non availability of relevant file and that later on he was informed by respondent No. 5 that allotment of the respondent No. 1 was cancelled on 11th August 1994 and that the said plot has been allotted to the appellant therein on 11th August, 1994 and that respondent No. 1 said to have been informed as regard the matter of cancellation of his allotment letter and lease deed by mailing the letter dated 15th August, 1994 addressed to his village home at Mohammadpur, P.S. Kulaura, Moulavi Bazar. Thereupon attorney of the respondent No. 1 who was living in New York, informed him about the cancellation of the plot for non-payment of 4th instalment and that for not constructing residential house as per Clauses 3 and 4 of the lease agreement. The respondent No. 1 faxed an application to the respondent No. 2 (herein) on 2nd June, 1995 requesting him to look into the matter and to accept the 4th instalment and that to allow him to make construction in the plot. In reply to the fax of the respondent No. 1 dated 2nd June, 1995 sent from New York respondent No. 5 informed the writ petitioner that matter of cancellation of his plot was intimated to him by the letter of 15th August 1994 mailed at his permanent address-village Mohammadpur, PS Kulaura, Moulvi Bazar. 

 3. Respondent No. 1 challenged the legality of the memo dated 15th August, 1994 contending, first, that he was not at all informed by issuing notice at the address which was communicated to the respondent Nos. 2-5 by the letter dated 10th July, 1989; that his allotment of the plot in question in Shahjalal Housing Estate would be cancelled for nonpayment of 4th instalment and that for not making construction as per terms of the lease deed, second, that letter dated 15 August, 1994 was sent to the address which was not the address for communicating any information regarding the plot since 1989 and that after return of the said letter with the remarks of the postal peon that addressee resides in a foreign country no attempt was made to communicate with the respondent No. 1 at the address which was available to the respondent Nos. 2-5 since 1989, and lastly, that the action of the respondent Nos. 2-5 cancelling allotment of the respondent No. 1 lacked bonafide since allotment was cancelled on 11th August, 1994 and that on that very day the plot was allotted to the appellant in the absence of any application from her side seeking allotment of a plot in Shahjalal Housing Estate, Sylhet. It was also contended by the respondent No. 1 that the allotment was made without making an advertisement in the newspaper inviting application from the intending seekers of allotment. 

 5. The High Court Division made the Rule absolute upon observing that in spite of knowing the last address of the petitioner the cancellation letter was addressed to his village home (writ petitioner-respondent No. 1 by the letter dated 10th July, 1989 informed the respondent Nos. 2-5 of his address for communication as regard the matter of his plot at Shahjalal Housing Estate and that he received communication from the respondent Nos. 2-5 up to 1991 at his address in USA) and that not only that decision as to cancellation though was taken on 11th August, 1994 and on the same date the plot was allotted in favour of the respondent No. 5 (appellant herein) and without making any attempt to circulate the order of cancellation in the newspaper and that the payment of 4th instalment was refused without justification and that possession that was delivered to the writ-petitioner was not at all taken from him and, as such, the same could not be redelivered unless the delivery was taken back from the writ petitioner and that resort to the provision of Clause 4 which gives right to terminate the lease in case of failing to complete construction of building within the stipulated time as in Clause 3 of lease deed "ought to be exercised according to law" and "thirdly, all actions could be set at naught if the same be malafide. In this case, we have noticed that the cancellation of the deed of lease and also the allotment in favour of the respondent No. 5 appears to have been done on the same day without application of respondent No. 5 would show that the action of the respondent No. 4 is tainted with malafide and such action is liable to be declared illegal and unlawful. And lastly, the notice has to be served upon the petitioner at the last known address as evidenced from Annexure-F and this has not at all been controverted and, as such, the impugned order of cancellation when the same has not been served upon the petitioner is wholly illegal and cannot be acted upon." 

 6. Being dissatisfied with the judgment and order of the High Court Division the writ-respondent No. 5, filed the petition for leave to appeal. Leave has been granted to consider the submissions that admittedly respondent No. 1 having not made any construction on the demised plot within the stipulated time and having not prayed for extension of time, the lease was liable to cancellation and the Housing Estate Authority having issued notice in the address of respondent No. 1 as mentioned in the agreement of lease, the High Court Division was wrong in holding the cancellation of lease to be without lawful authority,  that the Housing Estate Authority having power to cancel the lease on the happening of specified event and such event having happened, the High Court Division was wrong in holding the cancellation of the lease in question to be malafide merely because after passing the order of cancellation of lease the Housing Estate Authority allotted the plot in question to the appellant on the same day, that respondent No. 1 having left the country without making any arrangement for receiving notices in the address which he gave in the agreement of lease, respondent No. 1 cannot complain of non receipt of notices when those notices were sent by registered post in the address mentioned in the agreement of the lease and were returned unserved in the absence of respondent No. 1 and in such circumstance the High Court Division was wrong in finding the impugned order of cancellation as bad for non-service of notice. 

 7. It was asserted by the respondent No. 1 in his application dated 2nd June, 1995 addressed to the respondent No. 2 that he has been residing in USA since September, 1985 and used to receive letter from the office of the Administrative Officer, Shahjalal Housing Estate, Sylhet up to 1991 in his US address intimated by him by the letter dated 10th July, 1989 and since thereafter he did not receive any letter from the Shahjalal Housing Authority. It was further stated in the said letter that Shahjalal Housing Estate has the US address of the writ-petitioner in its record since he by his letter dated 10th July, 1989 intimated his address in US for communication with him as regard the matter relating to the plot allotted to him by the Shahjalal Housing Estate, Sylhet. 

 8. The notices of the Rule obtained by the writ petitioner-respondent No. 1 were served upon writ respondent Nos. 1-4 (personnel of the Shahjalal Housing Estate) but the said respondents did not enter appearance in the Rule and denied the fact of intimation of the address of respondent, No. 1 in USA in 1989 and of making communication with the respondent No.1 by the respondent Nos. 2-5 herein up to 1991 in connection with matter of plot allotted to respondent No.1 in the Shahjalal Housing Estate. It is seen from the Annexures K and K-1 to the writ petition that a letter was addressed on 13th May, 1993 to the village home of the writ-petitioner intimating him that time for payment of 4th instalment has expired and that he has also not started construction in the plot allotted to him and that by the said letter the writ-petitioner was asked to make the payment of the entire amount that has fallen due and also that in case of non-starting of construction allotment of the plot in question of the lease deed in respect Of the plot allotted would be cancelled without further communication. Thereafter, the writ respondent Nos. 1-4 (herein respondent Nos. 2-5) as seen from Annexure-L and L-1 to the writ petition cancelled the allotment of the respondent No. 1 on 11th August, 1994 and that sent a letter communicating cancellation of the plot and the lease deed to the village address of respondent No. 1. 

 9. The respondent Nos. 2-5 although made communication with the respondent No. 1 as regard the matters of plot No. 17 of Shahjalal Housing Estate till 1991 at the US address as per respondent No. 1's letter dated 10th July, 1989 but still then sent notice dated 13th May, 1993 asking the respondent No. 1 to pay the armor amount of 4th instalment and that to start construction as per terms of the lease to his village home. 

 10. In July, 1989 respondent No. 1 made available to the Shahjalal Housing Estate authority his address to communicate with him in his US address in respect of the matter of the plot No. 17 and the Housing Estate Authority communicated with the respondent No. 1 up to 1991. In this background of the facts the contention of the appellant, who of course is not legally competent to contend so since respondent Nos. 2-5 have not denied the fact of communicating with respondent No. 1 in his US address as regard matters of the plot No. 17 of the Housing Estate, that the respondent No. 1 left Bangladesh without making arrangement for receiving communication in the address given in the lease agreement is not well founded one as because the respondent No. 1 informed the Shahjalal Housing Authority in July, 1989 his address for communication with him relating to the matters of his plot in the Housing Estate and that the Housing Estate Authority communicated with respondent No. 1 up to 1991 at the address in USA given by the respondent No. 1. Admittedly, neither the notice asking the petitioner to pay the arrears of the 4th installment and that to start construction within 30th June, 1993 was not addressed to the respondent No. 1 to his address for communication as regard the matters relating to the plot No. 17 of the Housing Estate. The same being the undisputed fact the contention of the respondent No. 1 that his allotment of Plot No. 17 of Shahjalal Housing Estate was cancelled without intimation to him is found to be correct and because of that the order cancelling the allotment and the lease agreement in respect of the Plot No. 17 of the Housing Estate have quite legally been declared illegal by the High Court Division. Although the respondent Nos. 2-5 did not enter appearance in the Rule that was issued in Writ Petition No. 1289 of 1996, yet the record as being maintained in the office of the respondent Nos. 2-5 in connection with the Plot No. 17 of the Shahjalal Housing Estate allotted to the petitioner was placed before the High Court Division and the learned Judges of the High Court Division on scrutiny of the papers maintained in the file noticed that there was no application by the respondent No. 5 appellant on 11th August, 1994 seeking allotment of plot in the Homing Estate. There is also another glaring fact that respondent No. is allotment of the plot was cancelled on 11th August, 1994 and that Shahjalal Housing Estate Authority allotted the said plot No. 17 to the respondent No. 5 appellant on that very day in the absence of any application from her side seeking allotment of plot in the Shahjalal Housing Society. It is an undisputed position that allotment was made without making any public notification calling for applications for allotment of the plot in question that was available to the Housing Estate upon cancellation of the allotment of the respondent No. 1. The High Court Division also noticed that notice calling upon the respondent No. 1 to pay the arrears amount that had fallen due because of non-payment of 4th instalment and that for starting construction by 30th June in default whereof the allotment would be cancelled without further communication was sent to the village address of the respondent No. 1 and that letter intimating cancellation of the plot and lease thereof was sent to the village address of the respondent No. 1 although the Housing Estate had in its record as back as from 10th July, 1989 address of the respondent No. 1 in USA for communication relating the matters of Plot No. 17 of the Shahjalal Housing Estate and that the Housing Estate authority communicated with the respondent No. 1 in his US address up to 1991 as regard the matters relating to the Plot No.17 of the Housing Estate. 

 11. In the background of the aforesaid facts the High Court Division held the action of the Housing Estate relating to the cancellation of Plot No. 17 that was allotted to the respondent No. 1 as malafide. In our view the High Court Division has committed no illegality in the background of the fact as stated herein before in arriving at the finding that action of the Shahjalal Housing Authority as regard cancellation of the allotment of Plot No. 17 which was allotted to the respondent No. 1 was malafide. 

 12. The learned Counsel appearing for the appellant in the face of the undisputed fact as was in Annexure-F to the writ petition relating to making available to the Housing Estate authority address of the respondent No. 1. for making communication relating to the matter of Plot No. 17 of Shahjalal Housing Estate and that the Housing Estate Authority having had communicated with respondent No.1 up to 1991 at his address in USA that was made available on 10th July, 1989 and that in spite of that the Housing Estate Authority sent the letter dated 13th May, 1993 asking the respondent No. 1 to clear the arrears had fallen due against 4th instalment and that to start construction by 30th June in case of failure whereof allotment of the respondent No. 1 would be cancelled was addressed to respondent No. 1's village home and that letter intimating cancellation of the Plot No. 17 that was allotted to the respondent No. 1 was sent to his village home address and that allotment to the respondent No. 5, appellant was made on the very day of cancellation of the allotment of the respondent No. 1 without having any application of the said respondent No. 5 finds it difficult to support the action of the respondent Nos. 2-5 as regard cancellation of allotment of respondent No. 1. The other contention of the learned Counsel for the appellant that the High Court Division was in error in, holding the cancellation of the allotment of the respondent No. 1 without lawful authority as because the said respondent did not start construction as per stipulation in the. lease deed and that he having had not also applied for extension of time is not sustainable in the background of the material on record since as seen from the action of the respondent Nos. 2-5 that merely because of non-starting of construction in the plot allotted within the stipulated time, the allotment is not liable to be cancelled straight away but authority may proceed for cancellation after giving notice to the allottee and in that regard the Housing Estate Authority sent a notice to the respondent No. 1 fixing date with which respondent No. 1 was directed to start construction and that in case of default without further communication allotment and lease agreement would be cancelled to the address which to the very knowledge of the respondent Nos. 2-5 was not the address for communication with the respondent No. 1 in connection with the matter relating to Plot No. 17 that was allotted by the said respondents to the respondent No. 1. In the background of the facts the High Court Division was quite correct in holding that cancellation of allotment and the lease deed of the respondent No. 1 in respect of Plot No. 17 of Shahjalal Housing Estate were without lawful authority since the same were done without giving any notice to the allottee, the respondent No. 1.
